option_feedback.A: This is mass multiplied by speed, so the time power is one too small in magnitude.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Force is mass multiplied by acceleration, giving kg m s^-2.
option_feedback.C: This is the base-unit form of energy, not force.
option_feedback.D: Length belongs in the numerator for force, not the denominator.

questions.unit_policy: No written unit is required because the learner selects one complete option.

marking_points.text: Selects kg m^-3 as the SI base-unit form of density

option_feedback.A: Correct. Dividing kg by m^3 gives kg m^-3.
option_feedback.B: This multiplies by volume instead of dividing by it.
option_feedback.C: The reciprocal has been applied to mass as well as volume.
option_feedback.D: Volume has unit m^3, so the exponent must be -3 rather than -1.

marking_points.text: Selects kg m^-2 s^-1 as the SI base-unit form of k

option_feedback.A: Correct. Dividing kg m s^-2 by m^2 times m s^-1 gives kg m^-2 s^-1.
option_feedback.B: The denominator metre powers must be subtracted rather than added to the numerator power.
option_feedback.C: This does not include the full area-times-speed denominator.
option_feedback.D: This is the base-unit form of power and results from a different relationship.
